    • When a project was removed from the recent projects list or when project files were deleted, especially for missing projects (where the underlying folder was deleted or moved externally) or when Windows backslashes (\) vs forward slashes (/) differed, the backend threw filesystem errors or the frontend encountered unhandled promise rejections while attempting to open stale manifests.   3. Graceful Deletion of Missing Projects (crates/sb-core/src/project/mod.rs):
    • delete_project_files() checks if the folder exists and contains street-builder.json. If the folder is already missing on disk, it drops the entry from recent-projects.json cleanly without throwing an unhandled error.
  4. State Machine & Active Project Transition (src/features/projects/model/projectsStore.ts):
    • removeProjectFromList() and deleteProjectFiles() safely reset active selection and manifest in framesStore if the removed project was currently open. It then automatically opens the next available non-missing project or clears workspace cleanly.

Summary

The map view fails to load and remains blank when running the packaged desktop application (production build), even though it displays properly during development.

User Impact

When opening a project, users cannot see the map preview, GPS route path, or camera positions/markers in the installed app.

What Happened

The map engine relies on a background helper (worker) to process and render map graphics. When packaging the app for release, this helper file was not included in the application bundle. As a result, the map was unable to start and showed a blank screen.

Expected Behavior

The interactive map should load and display routes, tiles, and markers consistently in both development and installed desktop builds.

issues.display_title: Issue #29: Show popup message close app
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Summary

Replace the previous behavior (which strictly blocked window close with a toast warning during active uploads or media ingest) with an interactive confirmation modal (CloseConfirmDialog).

When the user attempts to close the application while an upload or media processing task is in progress, a confirmation dialog appears warning that continuing will stop all running processes.

Behavior & Flow

  1. Trigger Condition:

    • Active uploads (isUploading && !isPaused) OR
    • Running media ingest / frame extraction (status === "running").
    • Note: Paused uploads do not block close (maintaining previous behavior).

  2. User Actions:

    • Keep Running / Cancel: Dismisses the modal; the application remains open and processes continue uninterrupted.
    • Quit and Stop Processes:
      • Sends cooperative cancellation (commands.cancelJob) to all active upload and ingest jobs.
      • Transitions modal to a non-dismissable waiting phase with an animated spinner and live accessibility announcement (aria-live="polite").
      • Polls backend job registry (commands.listJobs()) every 300ms until all target jobs are confirmed terminated and child processes (e.g. FFmpeg, ExifTool) are safely terminated.
      • Features a 10-second timeout safety valve to prevent hangs.
      • Once cleared (or upon timeout), programmatic window destruction (window.destroy()) closes the window cleanly without prompt loops.

Technical Implementation

  • Tauri Permissions: Added core:window:allow-destroy to src-tauri/capabilities/default.json to allow programmatic window termination.
  • Coordination Logic (src/app/lib/closeGuard.ts):
    • collectActiveJobIds: Aggregates active job IDs across upload and ingest stores.
    • cancelActiveJobsAndWait: Orchestrates dispatching cancellations and polling backend registry as authoritative source of truth.
  • State Machine Hook (src/app/hooks/useCloseGuard.ts):
    • Intercepts onCloseRequested from Tauri window API.
    • Implements re-entrancy prevention on confirm action and proper listener unmount cleanup.
  • UI Component (src/app/components/CloseConfirmDialog.tsx):
    • Built with Radix UI AlertDialog for focus trapping and accessibility.
    • Locks Escape key and outside dismissal during the stopping phase.
  • i18n Localization:
    • Added 5 new localization keys (close_confirm_title, close_confirm_description, close_confirm_quit, close_confirm_keep_running, close_confirm_stopping) across all 15 supported locales (en, de, da, es, fr, it, jp, nl, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sv, zh).
    • Cleaned up obsolete toast notification strings.

Verification

  • pnpm lint (ESLint & Prettier passing).
  • pnpm build (TypeScript strict check & Vite bundle successful).
  • cargo check (Rust backend compiles cleanly with capability changes).

When users attempt to close the application while an upload or media extraction task (e.g. Timelapse Ingest) is in progress, a dialog warns that quitting will terminate running background jobs.

issues.display_title: Issue #36: fix(gps): Align total distance, selected frame count and map markers with Electron
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Before

After

Description

Video Info reported 6911 Meter and 72 selected frames for the project Crop, where the Electron app reports 107 Meter and 17 for the same video and the same GPS setting (5 Meter). The map also drew its distance dots away from the blue route line, left the first dot unconnected, and let the dots drift while the map was dragged.

The Electron app is the reference for all of these numbers.

Root Causes

  1. GPS track was never trimmed to the clip. An Insta360 .gpx sidecar covers the whole recording session. For Crop that is 1511 points across 28 minutes (6911 m), while the exported video is 60 seconds. Electron trims the track when it loads it (open.js:315-390): points sharing a timestamp collapse to the middle one, repeated coordinates are skipped, and the walk stops once the second counter passes the clip duration — 61 points, 107 m. The Tauri port loaded all 1511 points.
  2. Total distance was read off the wrong point. Electron assigns totalDistance on every walked coordinate, outside the spacing gate (measure-distance.js:148), so it is the route length at the last walked coordinate. The port used the distance of the last published marker, which stops earlier whenever trailing points fail the gate.
  3. Selected frame count used the published set. Electron shows selectLayer.length — the raw walk entries in GPS mode, the every-nth list in layers mode. The port showed the valid, deduplicated publish set, which is smaller.
  4. Marker coordinates were resolved against the wrong list. KeptPoint.track_index counts the filtered coordinate list in GPS mode, but the IPC layer used it to index the raw track, so the dots landed on unrelated points. The blue line was drawn from the raw track rather than through the markers (Electron's createLinesFromMarkers), and an Insta360 slice(1) left the first dot unconnected.
  5. Marker hover animated transform. MapLibre positions markers with an inline transform, so a CSS transition on that property made every dot lag behind the map while panning.

  • src-tauri/src/commands/projects.rs: markers report their own coordinate; the unused route field was removed from the IPC result.
  • src/features/map/components/MapCanvas.tsx: the route line is built from the markers, with no marker dropped.
  • src/features/map/styles/marker.module.scss: hover uses a box-shadow ring instead of transform: scale().
  • src/features/projects/components/VideoInfoModal.tsx: selected frame count follows selectLayer; feet use Math.floor(m / 0.3048) as convertMetersToFeet does.

issues.display_title: Issue #38: fix(auth): Stop the macOS keychain prompt on every app launch
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Description

macOS asked for keychain access every single time the app was opened, and choosing "Always Allow" did not stop the prompt from coming back on the next launch.

Root Cause

macOS binds a keychain item's ACL to the code signature of the binary that created it. The app binary is ad-hoc, linker-signed:

Identifier=street_builder-c33f1a6708685f89
CodeDirectory ... flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed)
Signature=adhoc
TeamIdentifier=not set

An ad-hoc signature carries no stable identity, so the ACL falls back to the binary's cdhash. Every rebuild produces a new cdhash and a new identifier suffix, so the item stored by the previous build never matches the running one and macOS prompts again. "Always Allow" only ever applied to the build that was running at the time.

Changes Made

  • src-tauri/src/session_store.rs (new): FileSessionStore writes the session (identity + bearer token + expiry) as session.json in the app data dir — ~/Library/Application Support/com.streetbuilder.app/ on macOS — with 0600 permissions. A corrupt file reads as "no session" rather than failing the launch.
  • src-tauri/src/keychain.rs: removed, along with the keyring dependency.
  • src-tauri/src/state.rs: AppState builds the store from app_data_dir.
  • crates/sb-core/src/auth: documentation updated; the SessionStore trait itself is unchanged, so the token still never crosses the IPC boundary.

Trade-off

The token is no longer encrypted at rest. It is protected by file permissions alone, so anyone able to read this account's home directory can read it. This was chosen deliberately over prompting on every launch.

Upgrade Note

Existing users are logged out once and sign in again. The old com.streetbuilder.app keychain entry is no longer read and can be deleted by hand.

Verification

cargo test -p street-builder covers the round trip, clearing twice, the 0600 permission bit, and the corrupt-file path. cargo check -p street-builder and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets are clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #41: fix(upload): Reupload keeps failing after a signal drop even when the connection is back
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Description

When an upload loses signal partway through, the project ends in the Upload Failed — N image(s) failed to upload state. Pressing Reupload (N) after the connection is back to normal still fails, and nothing is uploaded. The card only shows the generic "Upload Failed" message, so the user cannot tell why.

Observed on project Crop (1799 frames, GPS mode, 5 ft spacing): 13 frames uploaded, 4 failed (1549, 1611, 1673, 1797). Reupload never recovered.

Root Cause

The reupload job stops at its first step, check_upload_permission. The manifest supports this:

  • upload.status stays partial. Step 2 of run_upload would have written uploading if the job had got that far.
  • The frame files keep their original mtime. Step 5, the EXIF re-tag, never ran.

The permission check, get_upload_token and create_tour all use the shared GothruClient HTTP client (crates/sb-core/src/gothru/mod.rs). That client was built with no timeout and with the default keep-alive connection pool. When the signal drops, the pool keeps dead sockets. issues.display_title: Issue #43: fix(network): Show human-readable messages instead of raw HTTP errors
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Description

Error messages from HTTP requests reach the user in technical form. A wrong email or password on the login screen shows HTTP 404: There is no user found with this username and password. Other failures show text such as HTTP 500, creating tour: error sending request for url (...) or Upload token unavailable. The status codes, URLs and internal step names mean nothing to the user.

Root Cause

Every HTTP error became an SbError::Network(String) built from technical data, and the frontend (parseErrorMessage) displays detail as it is:

  • parse_json in crates/sb-core/src/gothru/mod.rs formatted error responses as HTTP {status}: {detail}, or as HTTP {status} when the body had no JSON message.
  • Transport errors (no connection, timeout, a dropped connection) used reqwest::Error::to_string(). That text includes the URL and the OS error. Several call sites also added an internal prefix, for example creating tour:, lookup place: or uploading frame:.
  • A response body with an unexpected shape produced unexpected response shape: <serde error>.

Changes Made

  • crates/sb-core/src/gothru/mod.rs
    • When the server sends a readable message, only that message is shown, without the HTTP xxx: prefix.
    • status_message(status): human text for an error status that has no server message. It covers 400, 403, 404, 408/504, 429, 5xx, and a generic fallback for anything else. 401 still maps to Unauthenticated.
    • net(e) is now pub(crate). It maps reqwest errors to human text for timeout, connection, decode and other failures. The raw error goes to the log through tracing::warn!.
    • A response with an unexpected shape now shows a human message. The serde error is logged.
  • auth/google.rs, upload/tour.rs, upload/places.rs, upload/queue.rs: all reqwest map_err calls go through gothru::net. The messages empty moderation_id returned and Upload token unavailable are rewritten in plain language.

Case Before After
